slides.say: Given: a squared plus b squared is equal to two a b plus nine. Which of the following is necessarily true?

So one given, two letters, and necessarily true. And the given looks balanced, a and b play the same role. That's a job for the mirror test we just learned, so let's start with it. [short pause] Then we'll prove it with algebra, and check it by plugging in numbers.
[short pause] Our first method, the mirror test. First, is the given a mirror? Swap a and b. b squared plus a squared is two b a plus nine. Exactly the same given.
So any pair that fits, its swapped pair fits too. Number one, a minus b is three. Swapped, b minus a is three. That's the opposite, so it can't always be true. Out.
Number two, a bigger than b. Swapped, b bigger than a. Opposites again, out.
Now the other mirror, flip all signs. Squares don't care about the sign, and minus a times minus b is a b. The same given again.
Number four, a plus b is three. Flipped, minus a minus b is three, so a plus b is minus three. Opposite, out.

And number three, the absolute value of a minus b. Swapped, it's the absolute value of b minus a, the same number. Flipped, minus a plus b in bars, the same again. It survives both mirrors. Number three is our answer, and we didn't solve anything.
[pause] Our second method, the algebra. a squared, b squared and two a b, those are the pieces of a shortcut formula. So let's move the two a b to the left side.
a squared minus two a b plus b squared is a minus b, all that squared. So a minus b, squared, is nine.
What squared gives nine? Three, or minus three. So a minus b is three, or minus three. In both cases, its absolute value is three.
at: So a minus b is three

slides.say: And that's exactly the trap in number one. It forgets the minus three.

[pause] Our third method, plugging in numbers. I need a pair that fits the given. Why b zero? Because then everything with b disappears, and a squared is just nine. So a is three or minus three. I'll take minus three, because a negative breaks more choices.

Number one, minus three minus zero is minus three, not three. Out. Number two, is minus three bigger than zero? No, out. Number four, minus three plus zero is minus three, not three. Out. And number three, the absolute value of minus three is three. It stays.

Which way is better? The mirror test found it in seconds, the algebra proves it, and plugging in is the safety net. So with a balanced given, try the mirror first. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: plugging in is the safety net
